$comment: A COMMITTED COPY of this repository's GitHub Actions allowlist, so a gate can
answer offline a question that otherwise only CI can answer -- and only after a
push, and only as an action-resolution error that names no secret at all.
IT COST A CI ROUND TO LEARN. rediacc/console is `allowed_actions: selected`, and
the Bitwarden composite's pinned sm-action was not on the list. Run 33690518859
failed at 'Initialize' with:
The action bitwarden/sm-action@1238aae8... is not allowed in rediacc/console
because all actions must be from a repository owned by rediacc, created by
GitHub, verified in the GitHub Marketplace, or match one of the patterns: ...
Nothing in the tree could have said so: the constraint lives in repository
settings. This file is that constraint, written down.
REFRESH with `npm run check:ci-actions-allowlist -- --refresh`, which reads
/repos/rediacc/console/actions/permissions/selected-actions. The network lives
there and nowhere else, so the gate itself needs no token and cannot degrade to
'passed' on a machine that lacks one.
WHAT THE GATE CANNOT SEE, said plainly rather than assumed away:
`verified_allowed` lets any Marketplace-VERIFIED creator run, and there is no
offline way to know who is verified. So an action that would be permitted only by
that route must be listed in `verified_exceptions` with the CI run that proves it
ran. Today that list is empty, which is the strongest state: every third-party
action in this repo is permitted by a pattern or by being GitHub-owned.
